newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba asset revaluation now seen without law change.
newsitem.headline: Buba asset revaluation now seen without law change.

text.p: Bonn's revised plan to revalue Bundesbank currency reserves means a fast-track scheme to change the Bundesbank law will now no longer be necessary, German balance sheet experts said on Thursday.

Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer had hinted at a banking conference in Interlaken in Switzerland on Wednesday that a law change might not be needed under Bonn's amended plan for a revaluation of currency assets, at the end of this year.
German Finance Minister Theo Waigel was forced to withdraw a plan for mid-year revaluation of gold and currency reserves under protest from the central bank.
Because the original plan also involved gold holdings, it would have required a change in the central bank law, which Waigel had hoped to push through before the summer break.

But a simple revision of currency reserve value can be met by making use of a clause in balance sheet law which allows reserves to be valued at a level higher than the all-time low, but sets the purchase price as an absolute maximum level.

While the central bank's 95 million ounces of gold are already in the balance sheet at the purchase price of 144 marks per ounce, the central bank's dollars are valued at the lowest ever Frankfurt fixing rate for the dollar of 1.3620 marks.

Although it is hard to assess the exact level at which dollar's currently held were first bought -- without close examination of the Bundesbank's books -- it is reasonable to assume that the central bank's holdings of about 65.7 million dollars were at least mostly purchased at a higher price.
This gap between the lowest historic price and the purchase price gives the central bank scope to revalue the holdings even under existing law, meaning no legal change is necessary.

The legal change was likely to have proved extremely controversial in the German parliament as the Bundesbank itself has made clear that it does not want to revalue its gold reserves until it becomes clear what method of valuation will be used by the European Central Bank.

But the central bank itself hinted at the possibility of revaluing other reserves in its initial statement protesting at Bonn's plans to force through an early revaluation of all reserves, which it termed an attack on it independence.

Protesting in part at the timing of the call for a revaluation, so far ahead of the planned start of European economic and monetary union in 1999, the central bank said in its statement that it would consider some changes in 1998.

"Following the decision on which countries will participate in EMU from the start, the Bundesbank will if necessary take account in its balance sheet for 1997 of a change in the risk situation on the basis of the existing law," it said.
The legal basis for the revaluation to go ahead is as follows.
Paragraph 26 of the Bundesbank law calls on the central bank to follow the rules laid out in German trading law (HGB) when drawing up its balance sheet.
Paragraph 280 of the HGB allows a company to raise the value of its reserves from the lowest historic price toward the purchase price when the lowest historic price is out of date.
The central bank is freed in its law of the obligation to do this, but has the option of doing so.

Given that the dollar traded at an average rate of 1.50 marks last year, and is now trading at about 1.72 marks, the central bank could probably make a good case for applying paragraph 280 to its books, the experts said.

An increase in the value of the dollar holdings to current market prices from the book level of 1.3620 marks would bring the total value of the holdings to 113.5 billion marks from around 89.5 billion currently, for a potential book profit of 24 billion marks, according to West-LB economist Irgeen Rust.

However it is unlikely that the dollars would be revalued to this level. If the central bank opted to increase the book value by 60 percent of the difference between the historic low price and current market prices, the potential profit would be 14.4 billion marks.
